info.title: 🌌 Aurora (the whole point)
info.content:
Yellowknife sits under the auroral oval and is one of the best places on Earth for the northern lights, and late November is peak season with long, dark, often clear nights.

- Best viewing ~10pm to 2am, away from town lights (Aurora Village, Prelude Lake, or a guided tour with heated shelters).
- You'll stand still for hours, dress for extreme cold.
- Cold kills batteries fast, keep spares in an inside pocket.
- Check Astronomy North / UAF aurora forecast and chase the clear nights.

info.title: 🎯 Our priorities
info.content:
Aurora: everyone, every clear night (a given).

Aush: Snowmobiling + night skiing
Eyan: Ice fishing + dogsledding
Kai: Wood bison viewing tour + dogsledding

Dogsledding is the group activity (2 of 3 want it). The schedule covers everyone's top two.

info.title: 🧊 Cold & daylight
info.content: Late November: highs around -15°C, lows -25 to -30°C, colder with windchill. Only ~6 hours of daylight (sun up ~9am, down ~3:30pm), so do activities early and save evenings for aurora. Frostbite risk in minutes on exposed skin, cover face, ears, hands.

info.title: 💱 Currency
info.content: Canadian Dollar (CAD), no exchange needed. Tap works most places, carry a little cash for spots like Bullocks Bistro.

info.title: 🍽 Eat & drink
info.content: Bullocks Bistro (Old Town fish shack, iconic), Dancing Moose Cafe (breakfast), NWT Brewing / The Woodyard (beer + food). Try Arctic char and local fish. Small town, arrive early.
